note: Curated concise descriptions; missing fields are unknown. Sources are descriptive evidence, not venom-to-phenotype relationships.

traits.head: Triangular head with contrasting pale facial lines.
traits.pattern: Adults dark with pale dotted markings; juveniles have clearer crossbands.
traits.variation: Young animals have a yellowish tail tip.

traits.pattern: Brown crossbands on a lighter ground; head copper-colored.
traits.caveat: Account uses the historical southern-copperhead subspecies name; retain geographic scope.

traits.pattern: Dark adults can obscure earlier crossbanding.
traits.special: Pale mouth interior exposed during defensive gaping.
traits.caveat: Historical range statements may include the separately recognized Florida cottonmouth; do not transfer its photographs automatically.

traits.head: Dark triangular head with contrasting pale stripes.
traits.variation: Young animals have brighter body pattern and a yellow tail tip; adults darken.

traits.pattern: Green dorsum in the Hong Kong account.
traits.caveat: Regional description; other populations need separate documentation.

traits.pattern: Brown to purplish-brown, plain or mottled; pale scales may be scattered.
traits.ventral: Brown to creamy-white depending on individual.

traits.pattern: Conspicuous red-and-black bands in the southern form.
traits.variation: Northern forms differ; historical subspecies treatment needs care.

traits.head: Rostral shield separates the internasals.
Very large and distinctly separated from neck.
traits.pattern: Dark rhomboids often merge into a wavy pattern on a pale ground.
traits.variation: The account reports no size difference between sexes.

traits.head: Pale edging or barring on the lip scales.
traits.caveat: Museum account covers three Austrelaps species; do not import larger-species dimensions as labialis measurements.

traits.pattern: Contrasting dorsal chevrons.
traits.caveat: Color and pattern vary regionally.
Dwarf-adder account includes other Bitis species; use only its caudalis section.

traits.special: Nasal scales can form a pair of short horns.
traits.caveat: Historical gabonica treatment may include western populations now assigned to B. rhinoceros.

traits.special: Prominent nasal horn cluster with multiple enlarged scale pairs.
traits.caveat: Horn arrangement differs from the shorter nasal projections described for gabonica.

traits.head: Head wider than body; vertical pupils.
traits.pattern: Yellowish to dark brown with optional mottled bands.
Brown to olive-brown; scales may have darker edges.
traits.caveat: Puerto Rico field account; cited 80 cm measurement is SVL, not total length.

traits.pattern: Yellow dorsal markings on a green background.
Predominantly green, without dark middorsal markings in the key.
traits.head: No black postocular marking in the keyed description.
Broad head distinctly separated from neck.
Flat head clearly separated from neck, pointed snout.
traits.variation: Females tend to be larger and more robust in the account.
traits.caveat: The Costa Rican account uses a historical schlegelii scope. Recent species-boundary proposals conflict; do not reassign catalog identity automatically.
traits.taxonomy: The eyelash-viper group has competing recent taxonomic treatments; historical locality and species scope require checking.

traits.pattern: Uniform ground color with variable middorsal designs.
traits.variation: Diagnosis includes lower ventral and caudal counts relative to the comparison population of schlegelii.

traits.pattern: Green with black mottling.
traits.head: Black postocular marking in the keyed description.

traits.pattern: Brown with pale-edged dark hook-like markings.

traits.head: Large triangular head, clearly distinct from neck; dark postocular bands.
traits.pattern: Brown, grey or olive with paired triangular flank markings.
traits.variation: Females grow larger than males.

traits.pattern: Brown, yellowish or grey with pale-edged trapezoidal marks.
traits.head: Dark postocular stripe.

traits.taxonomy: Historical northern-Venezuelan label within the disputed asper–atrox complex; do not automatically merge.
traits.caveat: Morphology and numerical size remain unpopulated until species scope is resolved.

traits.pattern: Greenish-brown with trapezoidal markings.
Reddish-brown with pale-bordered dark trapezoidal or crescent markings.
traits.variation: Distal tail white, especially conspicuous in juveniles.

traits.pattern: Reddish-brown to grey with irregular trapezoidal dorsal marks.
traits.head: Postocular stripe.

traits.taxonomy: Island-endemic species studied separately from continental Bothrops.
traits.caveat: Source is a genomics report; no appearance traits are inferred from that report.

traits.pattern: Highly variable brown to nearly black; dark inverted-V or hook-like designs.

traits.variation: Color changes with age and sex; juveniles are brown-toned.
traits.caveat: Adult male and female patterns require separate presets rather than one combined design.

traits.pattern: Grey or brown dorsum with dark inverted-V markings.
traits.variation: The regional account describes age-related color differences.

traits.ventral: Nearly unmarked pale belly in the original diagnosis.
traits.head: Pale upper labials and a less pointed snout than the atrox comparison.
traits.pattern: Pale-edged dorsolateral blotches.

traits.taxonomy: Species separated from other members of the former neuwiedi complex using qualitative morphology.
traits.caveat: Do not copy pauloensis or diporus facial patterns into this species.

traits.head: Dark pigmentation on the sides of the head is characteristic of the described pattern C.
traits.variation: Occasional pale supralabial spots occur.

traits.pattern: Light grey with dark zigzag-like dorsal blotches.
traits.head: Lance-shaped with a dark postocular stripe.

traits.pattern: Usually reddish-brown with darker dorsal markings.
traits.variation: Adult males and females differ in coloration; the study reports sexual dichromatism.

traits.head: Head spotting or mottling noted in comparison with asper.
traits.pattern: Dark trapezoidal markings.
traits.caveat: Traits taken from the explicit punctatus comparison, not the asper description.

traits.pattern: Black dorsal blotches or bands on white; belly unmarked white.
Alternating black and yellow rings continue onto the underside.
Dark body contrasts with red or orange head and tail.

traits.body: Triangular cross-section with enlarged vertebral scales.
traits.pattern: Narrow pale crossbands on dark body.

traits.caveat: Very similar externally to caeruleus; photographed clinical specimen is identified as cf. sindanus, not certain species identity.
traits.taxonomy: Keep uncertain identifications separate from confirmed morphology.

traits.head: Small head, little wider than neck.
traits.pattern: Blue-black dorsum with blue lateral stripes.
traits.ventral: Red; head and tail also red.
traits.taxonomy: Catalog spelling bivirgata is retained; account uses bivirgatus.
traits.caveat: Regional description; numerical proportions are not imported.

traits.body: Slender with a small, barely distinct head.
traits.pattern: Dark brown dorsum with red vertebral stripe.
traits.ventral: White with black bands; tail underside red with black bands.

traits.tail: Short, nonprehensile tail in the revised diagnosis.
traits.taxonomy: Historical godmani records can include populations subsequently split as sasai or wilsoni.

traits.head: Small but distinct, with postocular bands.
traits.pattern: Brown, grey or orange ground with approximately square reticulated designs.
Pale-bordered dark diamonds on tan to brown.
traits.tail: Often lighter than trunk with dark rings.

traits.head: Broad diamond-shaped head.

traits.pattern: Bright green.
traits.caveat: Distinguish from green boomslang and Philothamnus; shared color does not establish identity.

traits.pattern: Grey, brown or black body.
traits.head: White lip stripe.

traits.caveat: Specimen-level morphology is published under brevicauda. Measurements from individual vouchers must not be treated as species means.
traits.taxonomy: Name treatment differs; catalog label retained.

traits.caveat: Its texture must not be replaced by the smooth-scale template of Naja.

traits.pattern: Strongly contrasting dark upper surface and yellow underside.
traits.tail: Paddle-shaped tail with dark and pale markings.
traits.caveat: Museum account uses Pelamis platurus.

traits.pattern: Adults can be uniformly grey above and pale below.
traits.variation: Young animals have more conspicuous transverse bands.
traits.caveat: Western-range specimen study; age and regional variation remain relevant.
Retain species-specific scope rather than combining all bushmaster measurements.

traits.pattern: Yellow to pinkish or orange-brown body; upper head black.
Light brown or cream with dark rhomboids.
traits.head: Round snout profile.

traits.pattern: Greyish head; pale yellow, cream or salmon body with dark-edged scales producing posterior bands.
traits.caveat: Account uses ikaheka; existing lookup alias is ikaheca.

traits.head: Modest neck separation and a black head cap.
traits.pattern: Red, black and white or yellow rings.

traits.head: Black cap over much of snout and parietals.
traits.pattern: Narrow yellow rings border black rings between red regions.
Tricolored monadal body pattern; tail generally black and pale ringed.
traits.variation: Ring irregularities were frequent in the studied specimens.

traits.head: Rounded snout; little neck separation.
traits.pattern: Repeated short red-and-black or pale-and-black rings; head/tail may differ from trunk.

traits.head: Little neck separation.
traits.pattern: Complete red–cream–black–cream rings; pale rings may be white or yellow.

traits.head: More distinct neck in the description.
traits.pattern: Red, black and yellow rings.

traits.head: Black cap begins on the rostral.
traits.pattern: Study reports 12–21 black body bands.
traits.variation: Melanic populations are discussed.

traits.taxonomy: Complex revised using 358 specimens; spixii and obscurus recognized as separate taxa.
traits.caveat: Do not combine their historical color-pattern data automatically.

traits.head: Large head and blunt snout.
traits.pattern: Usually dark; hood marking variable or absent.
traits.caveat: Hong Kong description; retain regional scope and the neotype-based taxonomy caution.
traits.taxonomy: Neotype-based treatment distinguishes atra from regional kaouthia-like populations.
Former forest-cobra complex split using morphology and molecular evidence.
traits.caveat: Historical melanoleuca labels may include other forest-cobra species; locality matters.

traits.pattern: Brown with dark interstitial skin.
traits.ventral: Pale throat with dark bars or patches.
traits.head: Dark-edged pale cheek scales.
Rostral broader than high, visible from above in the examined Komodo/Flores material.
traits.caveat: Historical subspecies nomenclature; regional specimen description is not a range-wide color preset.

traits.pattern: Banded and patternless forms occur.
traits.variation: Color and pattern vary geographically; absence of bands is not automatically anomalous.

traits.pattern: Dark-edged pale body bands form part of the revised diagnosis of hannah sensu stricto.
traits.caveat: This appearance applies to the restricted modern concept; historical venom labels may cover other king-cobra species.
traits.taxonomy: The former broad king-cobra label was revised into four species in 2024.

traits.special: Supraocular projection wider than tall and contacting upper preocular in the key.
traits.caveat: Do not draw the tall horn of another Ophryacus species.

traits.pattern: Yellowish-brown with mostly rectangular dorsal marks in the comparison table.

traits.pattern: Yellowish-brown with rectangular or irregular patches in the comparative table.
traits.head: Unpatterned head in the comparison.

traits.pattern: Green; a brown vertebral stripe occurs in one reported pattern.

traits.head: Broad head with a high upturned rostral scale.
traits.pattern: Grey to reddish or dark brown with dark rectangular marks and a thin vertebral line.

traits.head: Distinct head and pointed snout in dorsal view.
traits.pattern: Brown or light grey with marks flanking a thin pale vertebral line.

traits.head: Elevated snout with a tall rostral in the holotype.

traits.pattern: Grey-brown with large dorsal blotches and smaller flank blotches in the observed snake.

traits.head: Broad, deep head with prominent cheeks.
traits.caveat: Keep juvenile build separate from adult build.

traits.body: Stout, with a fairly long tail.
traits.head: Broad, flat head; small round pupils.
traits.pattern: Usually glossy black, rarely brown.

traits.pattern: Complete red, black and white rings.

traits.pattern: Brown shades including ochre, chocolate and sometimes pinkish tones in the regional observations.

traits.head: Bright green head.

traits.pattern: Green; white lateral head stripe in the comparative table.

traits.pattern: Green or blue in the comparative table.

traits.pattern: Green with bluish lips; no postocular streak in examined specimens.

traits.head: Broad triangular head.

traits.head: Broad triangular head.

traits.head: Triangular head; vertical pupils.

traits.head: Slightly upturned snout ridge.

traits.head: Head lighter than body, with pale canthal and labial regions in the diagnosis.

traits.pattern: Chestnut to maroon.

traits.pattern: Often reddish or orange; other shades occur.

traits.ventral: Paler underside with possible dark bands or blotches.

traits.pattern: Pale dorsal shapes and pale, dark-bordered flank spots.

traits.head: Short head, wider than neck, blunt snout.

traits.head: Flattened with large symmetrical shields; no facial heat pit.

traits.head: Broad, flat triangular head distinctly separated from neck.

traits.tail: Relatively short; males proportionally longer-tailed than females in the study.

traits.taxonomy: Genus revised in 2012; historical Southeast Asian rynchops accounts can refer to schneiderii.

traits.taxonomy: Historical revision treats multiple lineatus forms; color-pattern scope must accompany locality.

traits.pattern: Grey to brownish or yellowish ground; dorsal pattern stronger at midline than flanks.

traits.head: Dull dark postocular stripe.

traits.pattern: Brown with dark triangular body marks.

traits.pattern: Dark markings become bands or chevrons posteriorly; a rusty vertebral stripe often occurs.

traits.pattern: Dark oval-to-round spots; tan, brown, grey or pale ground, often with an orange-brown vertebral stripe.

traits.head: Nine large symmetrical head plates.

traits.head: Broad triangular head distinct from neck.

traits.pattern: Black rings arranged in triads.
